fats.narration: 100g of fat. Cholesterol is 0mg, so one animal-fat downside is absent. Saturated fat is 13.8g, controlled for a pure oil, and polyunsaturated fat is 10.5g with 760mg of omega 3 adding backup. For oils and fats, the whole ranking mostly comes down to fat quality.

carbs.narration: No scored carb section here. Fibre, sugar, starch, and glycemic index are not applicable for this pure oil. For oils and fats, carbs are basically off the table, so this section does not move the ranking.

proteins.narration: No scored protein section here. Collagen, amino-acid scores, and protein digestibility are not applicable because there is no protein to judge. For oils and fats, protein is not the role.

vitamins.narration: Vitamin E is 93% DV, the clear vitamin strength. Vitamin K is 50% DV, so there is real backup too. Vitamin A is 0% DV, so this is not broad vitamin coverage. For oils and fats, vitamin E and K are the useful micronutrient story.

minerals.narration: Minerals are basically absent. Iron is 3% DV, the best number here but still tiny. Magnesium is 0% DV, and calcium is 0% DV too. For oils and fats, minerals rarely carry much, and they definitely do not here.

pros.narration: Pros first: brings polyphenols when fresh. The bitter, peppery quality is part of the real extra-virgin advantage. Mostly monounsaturated fat identity. That gives it a different fat-quality role from many seed oils and animal fats. Helps carry fat-soluble nutrients. A little oil can make vegetable-heavy meals work better.

cons.narration: Cons next: quality drops with heat, light, and age. The best part of extra virgin olive oil depends on freshness and storage. Extremely energy dense. It is still pure fat, so the calories arrive fast. Easy to overpour without noticing. Free-pouring can quietly add a lot more than intended.

closing.summary: Best bits are fat quality, vitamin E, vitamin K, and polyphenol upside. Weak spots are no carb or protein role, basically no minerals, and easy overpouring. Best for heart health, finishing food, and vegetable-heavy meals because the fat profile is strong, freshness matters, and a small amount can make vegetables work better.
